senses.gloss: A place where people live for a time in tents or temporary shelters.
examples: The refugees have lived in the *camp* for two years.
The soldiers set up *camp* beside the river.
Our *camp* was three tents and a fire ring.

senses.gloss: A group of people who share the same opinion or support the same side.
examples: The party split into two *camps* over the tax bill.
Both *camps* claim the poll proves them right.
She belongs to the *camp* that wants to start over from scratch.

senses.gloss: A person staying at a camp or sleeping outdoors in a tent.
senses.ru: отдыхающий в лагере; турист с палаткой
examples: Each *camper* gets a bunk and a footlocker.
The *campers* hiked to the waterfall before breakfast.
He was not a happy *camper* when he saw the repair bill.

senses.gloss: A narrow tube or passage inside the body.
examples: The dentist says I need a root *canal*.
Water got trapped in my ear *canal* after swimming.
A tiny *canal* drains tears from the eye into the nose.

senses.gloss: Something evil that spreads through a group and destroys it.
examples: Corruption is a *cancer* on the whole system.
He called the gangs a *cancer* eating the neighborhood.
Distrust spread through the team like a *cancer*.

senses.gloss: The hard, hollow, jointed stem of tall plants such as sugar or bamboo.
examples: Workers cut the sugar *cane* by hand.
The fence was built from split bamboo *canes*.
Raspberry *canes* have to be tied to a wire each spring.

senses.gloss: One of the four pointed teeth near the front of the mouth.
examples: The dentist capped a chipped *canine*.
Her upper *canines* came in crooked.
A wolf's *canines* can crack bone.

senses.gloss: A cloth cover fixed above a bed, a window, or an entrance.
examples: A striped *canopy* shades the tables outside the cafe.
The bed had a lace *canopy* over it.
Guests waited under the hotel *canopy* until the rain let up.

senses.gloss: A place at a workplace, camp, or military base where food is served.
examples: The crew eats lunch in the factory *canteen*.
The base *canteen* serves breakfast until nine.
We bought candy bars at the camp *canteen*.

senses.gloss: A lid or cover that screws or snaps onto a bottle, tube, or pen.
examples: Put the *cap* back on the toothpaste.
The *cap* on this bottle is too tight to twist off.
He lost the *cap* to his favorite pen.

senses.gloss: An upper limit set on an amount.
examples: The league plays under a strict salary *cap*.
Lawmakers set a *cap* on interest rates.
There is a *cap* of two tickets per customer.

senses.gloss: A playful adventure or a daring scheme, often a crime.
examples: The movie is a lighthearted bank-robbery *caper*.
Their midnight *caper* got them both grounded.
Police unraveled the whole *caper* in a week.

senses.gloss: The part of a spacecraft in which the crew rides.
examples: The *capsule* splashed down in the Pacific.
Four astronauts squeezed into the *capsule*.
The *capsule* separated from the rocket right on schedule.

senses.gloss: An officer of middle rank in the army, the police, or a fire department.
examples: A police *captain* runs the whole precinct.
He made *captain* after twelve years on the force.
The fire *captain* ordered everyone out of the building.

senses.gloss: Text on a screen showing what people are saying, for viewers who cannot hear it.
examples: Turn on the *captions* — I can barely hear the dialogue.
The video offers *captions* in Spanish.
On a live broadcast the *captions* run a second behind.

senses.gloss: One of the separate sections of a train.
examples: The dining *car* is at the back of the train.
Freight *cars* rolled past the crossing for ten minutes.
We rode in the last *car* of the subway.

senses.gloss: One of a set of stiff pieces of paper marked with numbers and suits, used to play games.
examples: He dealt each player five *cards*.
She keeps a deck of *cards* in the glove box.
Pick a *card* and do not show it to me.

senses.gloss: A small plastic rectangle used to pay for things or take out money.
examples: I paid with a *card* instead of cash.
The machine would not read my *card*.
Her *card* was declined at the register.

senses.gloss: A small stiff rectangle printed with information about a person or a right they hold.
examples: He handed me his business *card*.
You need a library *card* to check out books.
Show your ID *card* at the gate.

senses.gloss: A feeling of worry, or something that causes it.
examples: She has not a *care* in the world.
He left his *cares* behind for a week at the lake.
Money was the least of his *cares* that winter.

senses.gloss: As many people or things as a car will hold.
examples: A *carload* of teenagers pulled into the lot.
We took a *carload* of old clothes to the donation center.
Two *carloads* of relatives showed up for dinner.

senses.gloss: A reward offered to persuade someone to do something.
examples: The state dangled tax breaks as a *carrot* for new employers.
Management tried the *carrot* before reaching for the stick.
A bonus is a better *carrot* than a threat.

senses.gloss: The list of items you have picked out to buy on a website.
examples: I added the boots to my *cart*.
There are three items sitting in your *cart*.
She emptied her *cart* when she saw the shipping cost.

senses.gloss: A large criminal organization that produces and sells drugs.
examples: The *cartel* controls the smuggling routes near the border.
Two *cartels* have been fighting over the same territory.
He testified against the *cartel* leaders.

senses.gloss: A container or box made to hold and protect something.
examples: He snapped the guitar back into its *case*.
I dropped my phone, but the *case* saved it.
They carried in a *case* of bottled water.

senses.gloss: One person or animal that has a particular disease or injury.
examples: The county reported forty new *cases* of flu.
It turned out to be a mild *case* of food poisoning.
Doctors traced the first *case* to a traveler.

senses.gloss: A particular situation or example of something.
examples: In that *case*, we should leave early.
This is a classic *case* of bad timing.
There are *cases* where the machine simply stops working.

senses.gloss: The chess piece shaped like a tower, also called a rook.
examples: He slid his *castle* down the open file.
She traded a bishop for a *castle*.
The *castle* moves only in straight lines.

senses.gloss: Someone who pretends online to be a different person, usually to fool a romantic partner.
senses.ru: кэтфишер (человек с фальшивым профилем в сети)
examples: The man in the photos was a *catfish* using a model's pictures.
She realized she had been talking to a *catfish* for months.
Dating apps try to weed out *catfish* before anyone gets hurt.

senses.gloss: A group of lawmakers who work together for a shared cause.
examples: The freshman *caucus* pushed hard for the amendment.
She joined the bipartisan climate *caucus*.
Both *caucuses* met behind closed doors.

senses.gloss: An aim or principle that people work for and support.
examples: The bake sale raises money for a good *cause*.
She gave twenty years of her life to the *cause*.
Volunteers rallied to the *cause* overnight.

senses.gloss: A hollow space inside a body or an object.
examples: The surgeon opened the chest *cavity*.
Insulation fills the *cavity* between the walls.
Air trapped in the *cavity* made the wood sound hollow.

senses.gloss: The highest level that something is allowed to reach.
examples: Congress voted again to raise the debt *ceiling*.
The plan puts a *ceiling* on out-of-pocket costs.
She hit a *ceiling* on what that job would ever pay.

senses.gloss: A small locked room where a prisoner is kept.
examples: He spent twelve years in a *cell* with one small window.
Guards searched every *cell* on the block.
The *cell* held two bunks and a sink.

senses.gloss: A cellphone.
examples: Call me on my *cell* when you land.
Her *cell* died halfway through the drive.
He left his *cell* sitting on the roof of the car.

senses.gloss: One box in a table or a spreadsheet.
examples: Type the total in the last *cell*.
The formula pulls numbers from three *cells*.
Click the *cell* and start typing.

senses.gloss: A small group working as one part of a larger secret organization.
examples: Police broke up a *cell* operating out of the suburbs.
The movement worked in small *cells* that never met each other.
Each *cell* had its own leader and its own orders.

senses.gloss: A line of heavy metal links used to pull, fasten, or hold something.
examples: He locked his bike to the rack with a *chain*.
The tow truck hooked a *chain* to the bumper.
We put *chains* on the tires before crossing the pass.

senses.gloss: A group of stores, restaurants, or hotels owned by one company.
examples: A national *chain* bought out the local pharmacy.
The hotel *chain* has four hundred locations.
She would rather eat at a diner than at a *chain*.

senses.gloss: A series of connected events or things.
examples: One small mistake set off a *chain* of failures.
Investigators reconstructed the whole *chain* of events.
A *chain* of islands runs south from the mainland.

senses.gloss: The person who leads a meeting, a committee, or a university department.
examples: The *chair* called the meeting to order.
She was elected *chair* of the school board.
He is the *chair* of the biology department.

senses.gloss: The act or process of becoming different.
examples: There has been a big *change* in the weather.
She is ready for a *change* of scenery.
The new manager made a few *changes* right away.

senses.gloss: A television or radio station, and the number you tune to for it.
examples: What *channel* is the game on?
He flipped through the *channels* twice and gave up.
The news *channel* has run the same story all day.

senses.gloss: An official route through which information, money, or goods pass.
examples: Complaints have to go through the proper *channels*.
The company sells through three different *channels*.
We heard about it through unofficial *channels*.

senses.gloss: A simple tune in which words are sung on only one or two notes, especially in worship.
examples: The monks' evening *chant* echoed off the stone walls.
The service ended with a slow *chant* in Latin.
She recorded old *chants* sung in village churches.

senses.gloss: A local branch of a national club or organization.
examples: The local *chapter* meets on Tuesday nights.
She started a *chapter* of the club at her school.
Every *chapter* sends two delegates to the convention.

senses.gloss: A distinct period in someone's life or in history.
examples: Moving west opened a new *chapter* for the family.
That was a dark *chapter* in the country's history.
She is closing this *chapter* and starting over.

senses.gloss: A party game in which players act out a word or title without speaking, usually called charades.
examples: We played *charades* after dinner.
He acted out the whole movie title in *charades*.
*Charades* works best with a big group.

senses.gloss: A formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.
examples: He faces three *charges* of fraud.
The *charge* was dropped for lack of evidence.
She pleaded guilty to a lesser *charge*.

senses.gloss: The electricity stored in a battery.
examples: My phone still has a full *charge*.
This battery holds a *charge* for about a day.
The laptop lost its *charge* overnight.

senses.gloss: Money, food, or help given freely to people in need.
examples: He was too proud to accept *charity*.
The family lived on *charity* that winter.
They fed half the block out of pure *charity*.

senses.gloss: A map of the sea or the stars used for navigation.
examples: The captain spread the *chart* across the table.
Old *charts* put the reef in the wrong place.
He plotted the course on a nautical *chart*.

senses.gloss: The record of a patient's condition and treatment in a hospital.
examples: The nurse updated his *chart* after every visit.
Her allergies are noted at the top of the *chart*.
The doctor flipped through the *chart* before coming in.

senses.gloss: The weekly list ranking the most popular songs or albums.
examples: The single topped the *charts* for six weeks.
Their album fell off the *charts* in March.
Three of her songs are on the *charts* right now.

senses.gloss: The bill for a meal at a restaurant.
examples: Could we get the *check*, please?
He grabbed the *check* before anyone else could reach it.
The *check* came to forty dollars before tip.

senses.gloss: An act of looking at something to make sure it is right or safe.
examples: The job requires a background *check*.
Give the tires a quick *check* before you drive.
A spelling *check* caught the mistake.

senses.gloss: A small mark put beside an item to show it is correct or done.
examples: Put a *check* next to every name on the list.
The teacher left a red *check* beside each right answer.
Each finished task got a *check* in the margin.

senses.gloss: Something that limits or controls a power.
examples: The courts act as a *check* on the president.
The whole system rests on *checks* and balances.
Rent rules are one *check* on rising housing costs.

senses.gloss: A feeling of warmth and happiness, especially one that is shared.
examples: The lobby was decked out with holiday *cheer*.
A bowl of soup and some good *cheer* fixed him right up.
She brought *cheer* to everyone on the ward.

senses.gloss: An informal and often disrespectful word for a young woman.
examples: Some *chick* from accounting left you a note.
He calls every woman a *chick*, and nobody appreciates it.
A couple of *chicks* in the front row started laughing.

senses.gloss: A small hot pepper used to make food spicy.
examples: Chop one *chili* and drop it in the pot.
The sauce is made with dried *chilies*.
He grows six kinds of *chilies* in the garden.

senses.gloss: A hanging set of tubes or bells that ring when they move or are struck.
examples: Wind *chimes* clinked on the porch all night.
She hung a brass *chime* beside the door.
The shop sells *chimes* made from old silverware.

senses.gloss: A monster in Greek myth made from the parts of several animals.
examples: The vase shows a hero fighting a *chimera*.
A *chimera* has a lion's head and a serpent's tail.
*Chimeras* turn up all over ancient art.

senses.gloss: A small piece broken or cut off something larger.
examples: Wood *chips* cover the whole playground.
A *chip* of paint flaked off the door frame.
The recipe calls for a cup of chocolate *chips*.

senses.gloss: The small mark left where a piece has broken off something.
examples: There is a *chip* in the rim of this mug.
A stone left a *chip* in the windshield.
The table has a few *chips* along one edge.

senses.gloss: A tiny piece of silicon holding the circuits that run a computer or phone.
examples: The new *chip* runs twice as fast.
A shortage of *chips* slowed car production for a year.
This card has a *chip* you tap at the register.

senses.gloss: A small round plastic counter used instead of money in gambling.
examples: He pushed a stack of *chips* into the middle of the table.
Each *chip* is worth twenty-five dollars.
She cashed in her *chips* and went to bed.

senses.gloss: The range of things available to pick from.
examples: The menu offers a wide *choice* of salads.
There is not much *choice* in a town this small.
Buyers have more *choice* today than ever.

senses.gloss: The person or thing that is picked.
examples: That school was her first *choice*.
He was the obvious *choice* for the job.
Vanilla would not be my *choice*.

senses.gloss: The control that cuts down the air going into an engine to help it start.
examples: Pull the *choke* out before you start the mower.
The old truck will not turn over without the *choke*.
Push the *choke* back in once the engine warms up.

senses.gloss: A short, sharp downward blow with the side of the hand or with an axe.
examples: He knocked the board apart with one *chop*.
A karate *chop* to the neck ended the fight.
Two quick *chops* of the axe split the kindling.

senses.gloss: Any dull, tiresome task.
examples: Filing taxes is such a *chore*.
Getting the kids dressed became a daily *chore*.
Reading that manual was a real *chore*.
